Strict separation of the active normals from zero would add a uniformly positive slab to every near-active cap for the same small displacement; compactness gives a persistent positive gap on the remaining normals.

A finite positive balance gives a covering family of equal-mass caps, so the maximum depth of the full radial body equals the original optimum, not just the depth at the origin. The simplex optimum at an off-centroid point is excluded by its coordinate greater than 1/(r+1).

Conversely the gauge-profile ray identities give the centroid depth and the canonical vertex caps cover all candidate points with mass γ_r each. The positive projective chart maps halfspace traces in both directions and preserves their mass; degenerate whole-domain traces cannot lower the infimum.
